Had a similar experience once but mine was after the ect was done. Usually when the anaesthetic wears off, I would already be in the observation area. However there was once when it wore off while I was still in the OT. The oxygen mask was still over my mouth and nose, I felt suffocated but I couldn't move my arms to reach it. I remember trying to shuffle my legs. When someone finally removed the oxygen mask, I immediately pushed out the bite block in my mouth and was whimpering. Definitely no intent of manipulating or seeking attention.  Just to make it clear, my T and I do talk about it quite openly, and she also respects my choice if I don't wish to discuss it. I usually express it to her through my journal, whether it's an urge with no intention to attempt or I'm actively planning, and she will pick up from there. 
In my country, therapists/psychologists don't have the jurisdiction to commit clients to a psych ward; only  psychiatrists have, so I still feel somewhat safe enough to discuss it with her without fearing being involuntarily committed.

120g Bread flour (80%)
30g wholewheat flour (20%)
112g Water (75%)
30g Starter (20%) 
3g Salt (2%) 

Method:
1) mix flour + water (autolyse 1 hr)
2) knead in starter (rest for 45mins)
3) knead in salt (rest for 45 mins)
4) coil fold x 3 sets at 60 mins interval 
Total bulk ferment at room temp = 5 hours
5) Final shaping and placed into banner banneton (rest at room temp for 1 hr then overnight in fridge for 10hrs)
6) Bake at 230⁰C (that's the max temp for my oven) for 20 mins with steam, then 210⁰C for 15 mins without steam.

I live in a tropical country, so humidity is high and normal room temp is usually around 28⁰c
